title: Timed actions
preamble:
# Timed actions

The `after` continuation clause on a rule's
RHS. An `after <duration>: <actions>` clause schedules an action
list to run after a delay on the monotonic clock. The compiler lowers each
clause to a synthetic timer fact plus a follow-up rule; the
declarative core is preserved and no engine state changes are
required beyond ordinary fact assertion and retraction.

Paired with:
- [LGRA] for action grammar.
- [LLOG] for the `$ClockTick`
  substrate that drives timer firing.
- [LLEX.10.6] for the synthetic names
  timer facts take.
- [LCCO] for `on`,
  `timeout`, and `error` continuations on `call` actions; `after`
  composes with them per §7.

## What this is not

- Not a coroutine, yield, or await mechanism. `after` creates a
  follow-up rule, not a paused execution frame.
- Not a replacement for `timeout` per [LCCO.7], which fires when
  a call's response does not arrive. `after` fires on a delay
  regardless of any call state.
- Not a cancellation primitive. A scheduled `after`
  cannot be cancelled mid-flight. The supersedure
  mechanism at [LRST] puts
  `as <expr>` on `after` for per-fact supersedure on
  author-named keys (re-fire replaces the prior timer).
